test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill the tank in 21 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 24 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = (1/21 − 1/24) = (8 − 7)/168 = 1/168.

Time to fill full tank = 168 minutes.

Time to fill 1/4th tank = 168 ÷ 4 = 42 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 **Inlet Pipe**
 21
 168 units
 +8

 **Outlet Pipe**
 24
 −7

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** = 8 − 7 = 1 unit/min

⇒ **One-fourth of Tank Capacity** = 168 ÷ 4 = 42 units

⇒ **Required Time** = 42 units ÷ 1 unit/min = 42 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 42 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Efficiency of an **inlet pipe** is always positive, whereas the efficiency of an **outlet (emptying) pipe** is always negative.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Time taken = **Total Work** ÷ **Net Efficiency**. If net efficiency is positive, the tank fills; if negative, the tank empties.</p
